         ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA
   TRANSMISSION SERVICES CORPORATION’S RESPONSE TO INTERVENOR
 GEORGE NOELKE’S OBJECTION TO APPLICANTS’ LIST OF INTERVENORS WHO
         DID NOT FILE TESTIMONY OR STATEMENT OF POSITION

        Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC (Oncor) and LCRA Transmission Services

Corporation (LCRA TSC) (together, “Applicants”) file this response to Intervenor George Noelke’s

Objection to Applicants’ List of Intervenors Who Did Not File Testimony or Statement of Position

and Motion to Provide Notice and Opportunity for Hearing Before Intervenor Dismissal En Masse

(Noelke Objection). 1 For the reasons set forth below, the Noelke Objection should be overruled and

his motion to require Applicants to file a motion to dismiss should be denied.




        1
           Intervenor George Noelke’s Objection to Applicants’ List of Intervenors Who Did Not File Testimony or
Statement of Position and Motion to Provide Notice and Opportunity for Hearing Before Intervenor Dismissal En Masse
(May 17, 2026) (Item No. 4706) (Noelke Objection).


ONCOR AND LCRA TSC’S RESPONSE TO NOELKE OBJECTION                                                     Page 1
                                                 I.    RESPONSE

    A. Applicants complied with SOAH Order No. 6

        SOAH Order No. 6 established a procedural schedule governing this proceeding. 2 That

schedule expressly required Applicants to file a “List of Intervenors Who Did Not File Testimony or

a Statement of Position” by May 15, 2026. Applicants timely filed that list in compliance with the

procedural schedule and a corrected list on May 19, 2026. 3

        Mr. Noelke characterizes Applicants’ list as a “cloaked Motion to Dismiss.” 4 However,

SOAH Order No. 6 did not require Applicants to file a motion to dismiss, nor did it impose any

obligation on Applicants beyond compiling and filing the list. 5

    B. The ALJs have authority to dismiss non-compliant intervenors on their own accord

        Under 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) § 22.161, sanctions, including the limitation or

disallowance of a party’s right to participate in the proceeding, may be initiated sua sponte by the

presiding officer—meaning the ALJs may take it on their own accord without a formal request or

motion. 6 In other words, a motion by a party is not a prerequisite for the imposition of sanctions.

        From the outset, SOAH Order No. 1 put all parties on notice that every party must file either

testimony or a statement of position and that parties failing to do so would be dismissed and not

allowed to participate further. 7 SOAH Order No. 6 formalized and reinforced that warning by



        2
          SOAH Order No. 6 – Memorializing Prehearing Conference; Granting Good-Cause Exception; Extending
Comment Deadline on Application & Notice; Adopting Schedule; Setting Route Adequacy & Merits Hearings;
Addressing Procedures; Advising Intervenors on Dismissal at 5 (Apr. 20, 2026) (Item No. 788).
        3
          Oncor and LCRA TSC’s List of Intervenors Who Did Not File Testimony or a Statement of Position (May 15,
2026) (Item No. 4688); Oncor and LCRA TSC’s Corrected List of Intervenors Who Did Not File Testimony or a
Statement of Position (May 19, 2026) (Item No. 4766).
        4
            Noelke Objection at 1.
        5
            SOAH Order No. 6.
        6
            16 TAC § 22.161.
        7   SOAH Order No. 1 at 2 (Mar. 31, 2026) (Item No. 139).


ONCOR AND LCRA TSC’S RESPONSE TO NOELKE OBJECTION                                                    Page 2
 specifying that failure to comply with the filing deadline could result in dismissal. SOAH Order No.

6 stated:

             A party who fails to file either direct testimony or a statement of position is
             subject to being dismissed as a party. Accordingly, the ALJs hereby give notice
             that if an intervenor fails to file either written direct testimony or a statement
             of position by the prescribed deadline of May 13, 2026, the ALJs will dismiss
             them as a party unless that intervenor, by May 20, 2026, files a response
             setting forth good cause for failing to comply and requests a hearing on that
             issue. Intervenors who are dismissed will be prohibited from participating in the
             hearing on the merits and briefing. 8

        These warnings constitute the notice required under 16 TAC § 22.161(a). Moreover, 16 TAC

§ 22.124(a) expressly provides that the presiding officer may sanction any party who fails to comply

with the requirement to file testimony or a statement of position by the deadline, in accordance with

16 TAC § 22.161. The ALJs’ exercise of their authority under these rules does not depend on

Applicants filing a separate motion to dismiss.

    C. Intervenors awaiting a ruling on a request to intervene are afforded all rights and
       obligations of a party

        The Noelke Objection points out that the deadline for intervenors to file testimony or a

statement of position came two days before the ALJs ruled on the motions to intervene of a large

number of intervenors. However, under 16 TAC § 22.104, a person who has filed a motion to

intervene has all the rights and obligations of a party pending the presiding officer’s ruling on the

motion to intervene. 9 The ALJs included such instruction in SOAH Order No. 2 10 and various orders

thereafter. Accordingly, intervenors were not precluded from filing, and, in fact, were required to




        8    SOAH Order No. 6 at 13 (Apr. 20, 2026) (Item No. 788) (emphasis in original).
        9
             16 TAC § 22.104(c) (emphasis added).
        10
           See SOAH Order No. 2 – Granting Motions to Intervene (Apr. 9, 2026) (Item No. 343) (“Pending a ruling on
your motion, you have all the rights and obligations of a party.”).


ONCOR AND LCRA TSC’S RESPONSE TO NOELKE OBJECTION                                                     Page 3
 file, testimony or statements of position by May 13, 2026, notwithstanding the pendency of their

intervention request.

                                     II.   CONCLUSION


        For the foregoing reasons, Applicants respectfully request that the ALJs deny the Noelke

Objection in its entirety.



Respectfully submitted,
